title: Set, get, delete
hints: A record is just a dict of fields. The whole database is a dict of those: `dict[str, dict[str, str]]`.
`setdefault(key, {})` creates the record on first write in one line. For reads, `self.records.get(key, {}).get(field)` returns None for both kinds of missing.
In `delete`, check membership before removing so you know whether to return True or False. If the record's dict is now empty, `del` the record too.
Remember `""` is a valid value — never use truthiness (`if value:`) to decide whether a field exists.
